headline.text: Starting progesterone one day earlier raised the clinical pregnancy rate from 44% to 52%.
headline.payoff: raised the clinical pregnancy rate from 44% to 52%.

card.dek: 1,024 frozen single-blastocyst transfers, randomized. Day 5 start: 52%. Day 6 start: 44%. Protocol was otherwise identical.

beats.detail: The window of implantation opens roughly five days after progesterone begins.
All other protocol steps were identical between groups.
Day 5 blastocysts only; day 6 blastocysts were excluded from both arms.

hero.subject: a human blastocyst entering the uterine cavity with the endometrium highlighted
hero.prompt: Textbook watercolor illustration, off-white background: a cross-section of the uterine cavity with a single blastocyst descending toward a thickened, receptive endometrium. The endometrium rendered in warm pink layers. No text, no labels, no numbers.

card.evidence_boundary: Women undergoing frozen single blastocyst transfer at one centre. Day 6 blastocysts and natural cycle FET were excluded. The day-5 advantage may not apply to day 6 blastocysts.

takeaway.text: Ask whether a day-5 start is possible. The implantation window is narrow.
